Begin with the person, whose complete set of true attributes is has_debt, has_waiver, is_student, is_suspended. Every other predicate is false.

The policy can be read in five sentences. Rule r1 yields eligible when all of is_student hold. Rule r2 yields not_eligible when all of has_debt hold. Rule r3 yields eligible when all of has_debt, has_waiver hold. Rule r4 yields eligible when all of is_employee, has_manager_letter hold. Rule r5 yields not_eligible when all of is_suspended hold.

When their conclusions disagree, precedence is precise: r3 overrides r2; r5 overrides r1; r5 overrides r4. Only the listed priorities apply, between fired rules with opposite conclusions. A fired lower-priority rule is suppressed; the other fired rules remain active. Both eligible and not_eligible remaining active means conflict. Only eligible means yes; only not_eligible, or no active conclusion, means no.

items.text:
# Rule System Description for Future Receiver

## Overview

This system determines whether a person is **eligible** or **not eligible**, and can also report a **conflict** if rules contradict each other without a clear resolution.

---

## Possible Facts You May Assert

You may declare any combination of the following facts about a person:

| Fact | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `is_student` | The person is a student |
| `has_debt` | The person has outstanding debt |
| `has_waiver` | The person holds a valid waiver |
| `is_employee` | The person is an employee |
| `has_manager_letter` | The person has a manager's letter |
| `is_suspended` | The person is suspended |

---

## Rules

| Rule ID | Conditions (ALL must be true) | Conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| **r1** | `is_student` | ✅ eligible |
| **r2** | `has_debt` | ❌ not eligible |
| **r3** | `has_debt` AND `has_waiver` | ✅ eligible |
| **r4** | `is_employee` AND `has_manager_letter` | ✅ eligible |
| **r5** | `is_suspended` | ❌ not eligible |

---

## Priority (Conflict Resolution)

When two rules fire and produce **opposing conclusions**, the higher-priority rule wins:

| Higher Priority | Overrides |
|---|---|
| **r3** beats **r2** | A waiver overrides plain debt disqualification |
| **r5** beats **r1** | Suspension overrides student eligibility |
| **r5** beats **r4** | Suspension overrides employee+letter eligibility |

> ⚠️ If two conflicting rules fire and **no priority** is defined between them, the answer is **`conflict`**.

---

## Query

After asserting facts, ask:

> **"eligible?"**

The system will respond with one of:
- `yes`
- `no`
- `conflict`

---

## Current Known Fact

The system already has **`is_suspended`** asserted as a baseline fact.
